Thin, light interior lines are clearly visible against the grey fill; they radiate from a single convergence point located in the upper part of the outline — roughly one third of the way down from the top edge, slightly right of the outline's horizontal center as I read it. Spokes run from that point to the left corner, the right corner, the two upper corners, and the two lower corners. A very faint larger hexagonal silhouette is barely visible behind and below the surface. No text, numbers, or scale bars are visible.
2. Frame 2 shows the same scene: near-black background, a light grey elongated hexagonal surface with the same outline, size, and screen position, and thin light interior lines clearly visible against the fill. The difference is the convergence point: here it sits close to the middle of the outline — near its centroid, slightly above the outline's vertical midpoint as I read it — with spokes running to all six outline corners, including a nearly horizontal pair of lines through the left and right corners. The fill reads slightly more uniform than in frame 1; the background silhouette is fainter or not visible to me here. No text, numbers, or scale bars are visible.
3. Differences: the position of the interior-line convergence point. In frame 1 it is displaced toward the top (far) edge, about one third of the way down from it; in frame 2 it sits near the outline's center. In screen terms the convergence point in frame 2 is lower than in frame 1 by a small amount I cannot quantify precisely. The upper region of the surface in frame 1 reads as compressed thin facets and the lower region as larger facets; in frame 2 the six regions read as roughly symmetric. Apparent identicals: the outer outline, screen position, colors, background, line rendering style, and absence of any overlay or text.
4. Frame 1: the convergence point sits inside the outline, well above its visual center, closer to the top (far) edge than to the bottom (near) edge; I cannot say whether it is displaced vertically only, and my position reading has moderate uncertainty because the lines are thin. Frame 2: the convergence point sits inside the outline near its center — at the same level as the outline's vertical midpoint within my reading precision. I cannot convert either position into a height, and I cannot exclude small differences beyond what I can resolve.
5. There is no scale reference in either frame; the oblique perspective strongly foreshortens vertical offsets into small screen shifts; the interior lines are thin (one-pixel-scale) and low-contrast even with the edge-contrast presentation; the fill shading is a smooth lighting gradient; and the faint background silhouette offers no shared edges for calibration. Together these prevent any exact position, height, or distance determination.
6. The single most confusing aspect is the magnitude question: the convergence-point displacement between the frames is clearly visible in direction but not in magnitude — nothing in either frame lets me say how large the change is in any unit, and the faint background silhouette remains unexplained (floor, shadow, or backdrop). A secondary confusion is that the fill shading differs slightly between the frames, and I cannot tell whether that is lighting or geometry.
